profiles.name: tnboles77
profiles.profile: This file is basically two different golfers duct-taped together. The driver and irons keep filing noise complaints, but the wedges and putter have been showing up like the only adults in the room, which is why the net results keep looking way better than the ball-striking crimes suggest. With only two looks in the window, the story is still squishy, but the identity is obvious: if the tee ball gets dragged into the alley, the around-the-green work can still mug the card and drag him home.

profiles.name: CRANK
profiles.profile: This is the classic CRANK experience: the tee game kicks the table over, then the short game sneaks in wearing a fake mustache and tries to save the party. The profile is volatile as hell, because the irons have been decent in spots, but the driver keeps taking a vacation to somewhere stupid and forcing the rest of the bag to clean up the mess. When the wedges get hot, he can absolutely survive; when they don’t, the scorecard turns into a salvage operation with paperwork.

profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.profile: Dan94 is a full-on tee-to-green bully, the kind of player who looks like he’s trying to break the simulator and the course at the same time. The approach game is the engine, the distance is obscene, and the putter is just good enough that the whole thing doesn’t collapse into a lawsuit. The weird part is the net results are consistently a notch behind the gross damage, which is basically golf’s way of saying: congrats, you’re destroying the field, but the format still made you work for it.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.profile: KeithK75 keeps showing the same annoying truth: the irons are the headline, and the rest of the bag is mostly there to not ruin the scene. He’s got enough tee pop and enough touch to keep the rounds from getting stupid, but the best version of him is when the approach play is purring and the putter is just competent instead of trying to steal the whole damn show. The file is strong, consistent, and a little unfair to everyone else, which is rude in the best possible way.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.tagline: PUTTER DOING MOST OF THE HEAVY LIFTING
profiles.profile: MattF is the kind of dude who can make a round look very tidy without ever really bullying the place. The long game is solid, the putter is doing the main character work, and the whole setup has enough pop to threaten a lot of cards without needing miracles. There’s a small sample here, so don’t get horny about the certainty, but the identity is already readable: when the greens are rolling, this bag can absolutely fake a much bigger resume than it probably has.

profiles.name: HamSammich
profiles.tagline: SHORT GAME FIRE, EVERYTHING ELSE ON FIRE TOO
profiles.profile: HamSammich is a messy little science project: the short game has been the best part of the bag, the putter occasionally throws a bone, and everything from the tee through the middle of the green likes to make the round way harder than it needs to be. The result is a profile that lives on damage control and random rescue missions. When the around-the-green work is sharp, he can hang around; when it isn’t, the card starts looking like it got kicked down a staircase.
